title: Shop profile (public part)
description: What differs between shops and is safe for anyone to read. Hosting serves it as /shop-profile.js; the shop and the stockroom read it when the page opens. Plan, test mode, secret keys and sender domain are NOT here: they live in server-only documents and the platform registry. The payment form's public ids are (payments): the page needs them to show the card form.

version.description: Format version. Bump only with a change both apps can read.

shopId.description: The shop's id in the registry, also the project id suffix.

firebase.description: The Firebase web settings. Not secret.

databaseURL.description: The stockroom's Realtime Database address. Missing: the project's default database address.

siteUrl.description: The shop's address, no trailing slash.

appCheckSiteKey.description: Bot-protection site key. Empty or missing: the app's build setting is used.

stockroom.description: Where the stockroom keeps its data inside the shop's project (plan 1.20): its own named Firestore database and its own storage bucket, each with its own rules. Missing: the project's default database and bucket (a stockroom in a project of its own).

firestoreDatabase.description: The named Firestore database: "stockroom" for every shop setup makes.

switches.description: Features one press needed once that a new shop doesn't. Each is on only when true; missing means off. Setup writes all four as false.

legacyStockroomSignIn.description: The shop's admin sign-in also signs into a separate stockroom project.

githubPagesForwarding.description: An old GitHub Pages address forwards visitors (and their bag) to the shop.

gmailReceiptFinder.description: The stockroom's Gmail receipt finder and Gmail import.

gmailOrderScan.description: The stockroom's Orders screen reads order receipts from the publisher's Gmail through Apps Script.

payments.description: How the shop takes card payments, and the public ids its payment form needs. Missing: the shop's own keys in its settings (mode own). Setup writes it once the press's account exists (step 13). The server never trusts it: the platform's payment service acts only on the account the registry lists for the shop.

provider.description: Which provider takes the payments. The shop's server reads the same choice from SHOP_PAYMENT_PROVIDER.

mode.description: own: the shop's own keys, in its settings. platform: through the platform's payment service, on the press's connected account.

stripe.description: Stripe in platform mode: the press's connected account and the platform's publishable keys, public by design.
